newsitem.title: USA: US manufacturing sector grows solidly - NAPM's Ore.
newsitem.headline: US manufacturing sector grows solidly - NAPM's Ore.

text.p: The U.S. manufacturing sector is growing at a brisk pace, while inventories appear to be contracting, said Norbert Ore, chairman of the National Association of Purchasing Management's business committee.
The official spoke to reporters in a conference call shortly after the release of the June NAPM report, which dropped to 55.7 last month from 57.1 in May.
Ore also said the June NAPM survey showed no signs of inflation.
The NAPM official added that if the Federal Reserve was looking for signs of price rises as a reason to tighten monetary policy at its July policy meeting, the NAPM June report offered none.
"We're not seeing any signs of inflation and if the motivation to changes in interest rates is inflation, there aren't any signs in this report that we see," Ore said.
The Fed's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets on July 1 and 2 to deliberate on the nation's monetary policy.

Ore said the NAPM survey indicated manufacturers were optimistic about the performance of the economy in the second half of the year. He also said the manufacturing labor market was positive but did not look real strong over the long run.
